heading: RBI Cracks Down on Bank's "Dark Patterns" and Mis-selling
tldr: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued new guidelines to curb unfair sales practices by banks and financial service providers.
These guidelines specifically target "dark patterns" like forced bundling of products and hidden opt-outs in digital interfaces.
Banks are now mandated to ensure transparency, provide clear product information, and obtain explicit customer consent for all offerings.
The new rules aim to protect customers from mis-selling of unsuitable products and improve ethical conduct in financial services.
This move is expected to empower customers and foster greater trust in the banking system by preventing deceptive tactics.
caption:
Ever felt tricked into buying something you didn't need from your bank? 🤔 The RBI is stepping in to stop banks from using clever tricks, like hiding extra charges or adding products without your clear 'yes'. These new rules mean banks have to be super clear and fair with you. It's all about protecting your money and making sure you truly understand what you're buying. Read more about how this helps you.
